origin: 오너 지시(2026-08-18): 「새로 추가된 코퍼스 셋 사용을 가지고 1배치 돌려서 핸드오프해」
_★설계_핵심: v3.3 신규분(개념 9 + 장르라벨 20)은 지금까지 **출력층 관측**으로만 존재했다(Suno가 우리 렌더를 그렇게 불렀다). 이 배치는 그 어휘를 **입력층에 처음 써넣는 시행**이다. ⇒ 생성 결과를 재분석하면 우리가 여태 갖지 못한 **처방 대조군**의 첫 쌍이 생긴다. ★단 이것은 통제 실험이 아니다(대조군 없음·1회). 관측 기록용으로만 쓸 것.
_★정직_고지: 신규 개념 9건의 attested_count는 2~7로 **저표본**이고 confidence는 medium 8 / high 1이다. 이 배치가 잘 나와도 「신규 어휘가 작동한다」의 증거가 아니다 — 곡 성패에는 프라이어층(가사 정서·에너지·구조)이 함께 걸린다(L4 prior-bound).
_★게이트: scripts/v33x_batch_gate.py — G1 SP≤1000자 / G2 배정어휘 축자포함 / G3 명찰형0 / G4 v3.3 신규라벨 / G5 SP-필드 BPM·키 일치. 10/10 PASS(2026-08-22).
_★DB_genre열_주의: songs.genre 열은 build_handoff.extract_genre()가 SP 첫 문장을 'with/featuring' 앞에서 자른 값이라 v3.3 신규 라벨 전문이 아니다(예 #6 DB='Orchestral cinematic score' / 실제 처방='Orchestral cinematic score with a focus on woodwinds and strings'). ★처방 정본은 style_prompt 전문과 이 파일의 genre 필드다.

songs.title: 먼저 도착한 사람
songs.sub_theme: Sparse minimalist chamber-orchestral opener with solo cello, oboe and hall-reverb tenor vocal
songs.sp: Cinematic orchestral score. The piece opens with a solo cello playing a slow, legato melody in the tenor register, answered by a solo oboe carrying a bare counter-melody. A string section provides sustained harmonic pads in the background, moving in gradual volume swells with divisi violins in the upper register. Muted french horns add low, breathy swells beneath, while a grand piano places single sustained notes and sparse arpeggiated figures in the mid register. Orchestral percussion is restrained: a soft timpani roll and one suspended cymbal swell before the final section. The harmony rests on minor seventh and suspended fourth voicings, resolving late. Male tenor vocals enter in a soft, breathy delivery in the lower register, opening into a clear resonant chest voice as the strings rise. Long hall reverb on the vocal, cello and piano creates a spacious acoustic environment with a long natural decay. 62 BPM, D minor, 4/4 time.

songs.title: 빈 홀에서
songs.genre: Orchestral film score in 3/4 time at 100 BPM
songs.sub_theme: Chamber-orchestral cinematic waltz with intimate Korean male tenor vocals
songs.sp: Orchestral film score in 3/4 time at 100 BPM, in E minor. A chamber orchestra plays a slow waltz across an empty auditorium. Divisi cellos and double basses hold sustained root notes beneath the meter while first violins carry a legato melody with warm, unhurried vibrato. A solo harp arpeggiates upward on the third beat of each bar, and a felted upright piano marks the downbeat with soft, pedal-blurred voicings. Clarinet and french horn enter mid-arrangement with long swelling lines. The harmony leans on major seventh and added ninth colours, luminous and unresolved, drifting rather than cadencing. Timpani rolls arrive quietly under the largest phrases; no drum kit. Male tenor vocals sit close and intimate, breathy in the low register and opening to a clear head voice on high phrases, sung in Korean with gentle rubato. Production is natural and wide: hall reverb with a long decay tail, distant room mics, audible bow noise, ending on a sustained string chord fading to silence.

songs.title: 접이의자 여든두 개
songs.genre: Gypsy jazz quartet featuring solo clarinet, acoustic rhythm guitar, upright bass, and accordion
songs.sub_theme: Manouche swing with accordion, minor-key and wandering
songs.sp: Gypsy jazz quartet featuring solo clarinet, acoustic rhythm guitar, upright bass, and accordion, recorded live in an empty hall. The acoustic rhythm guitar drives a la pompe pulse — muted staccato chords on the off-beats, dry and percussive, comping under everything. Woody pizzicato upright bass walks in steady quarter notes while the accordion breathes long legato pads and counter-melodies behind the beat. Solo clarinet leads: warm and low in the verses, bright improvised runs and flourishes over the turnarounds, with light vibrato and melodic slides. Warm female vocals, close-miked and intimate, slightly breathy, phrasing lazily behind the beat. Harmony is minor-key and restless, leaning on sweetly unresolved sevenths that slide a step downward before settling home. Swung feel in 4/4 time at 168 BPM in the key of G minor. Clean acoustic production, natural room reverb with a long empty-hall tail, warm analog tone. Nostalgic, wandering, bittersweet.

songs.sp: Bossa nova jazz quartet recorded in a large empty hall after hours, warm and unhurried at 92 BPM in A minor, 4/4. A nylon-string acoustic guitar leads with soft rounded attack, playing rhythmic accompaniment with bossa nova comping patterns, its voicings built on major seventh chords that hang unresolved in the room. The upright bass carries melodic movement in the lower register, walking gently beneath the guitar rather than marking roots. Brushed drums stay quiet on the snare, dry woody cross-stick clicks marking the off-beats with almost no cymbal wash. Acoustic piano enters sparsely, answering the vocal with single-note lines and lush floating chord colors. Breathy female vocals sing close to the microphone in a restrained, conversational tone, slightly behind the beat, with audible breath and little vibrato. Production is intimate and analog: ribbon-microphone warmth, natural room reverb with long empty-hall decay, soft tape compression. Sparse, with silence between phrases.

songs.sp: K-Pop power ballad featuring a male tenor vocal, 72 BPM in B minor, 4/4. Opens nearly bare: close-miked upright piano with the sustain pedal held, arpeggiated figures ringing into a wide hall reverb, room tone audible between phrases. The male tenor vocals enter soft and breathy in the lower register, conversational and rubato. A string section swells at the pre-chorus, cellos legato beneath sustained violins; fretless bass and brushed snare join, still restrained. The first chorus lifts into chest voice over shimmering clean guitar arpeggios, and the chorus vocals are doubled for width. Verse two adds palm-muted guitar and eighth-note hi-hat. The bridge strips back to piano and voice alone, then a half-time tom build. The final chorus arrives with full band, driving drums, crash cymbals, overdriven power chords, soaring strings, and a strained belt with falsetto ad-libs. Outro decays to solo piano and a long reverb tail. Korean lyrics throughout.

songs.title: 먼지가 보이는 각도
songs.title_en: The Angle Where Dust Is Visible
songs.genre: Orchestral cinematic score with a focus on woodwinds and strings
songs.sub_theme: Woodwind-led cinematic miniature with wordless-quiet female alto and sustained string pads
songs.sp: Orchestral cinematic score with a focus on woodwinds and strings, 66 BPM in C minor, 4/4. A solo flute opens alone with a slow descending line, joined by clarinet in thirds and a low bassoon counter-melody. The string section provides sustained harmonic pads in the background, divisi violas and cellos moving in slow bow swells with almost no vibrato. A harp places single plucked notes at the end of phrases and a celeste answers an octave above. French horns hold soft, distant chords underneath. No drum kit: only a quiet timpani pulse and one suspended cymbal swell before the last section. The harmony moves between minor ninth and suspended second voicings and never fully resolves. Female alto vocals enter low and breathy in the middle register, restrained and almost spoken, sung in Korean with long pauses between phrases. The production is a spacious acoustic environment with a long natural decay, audible room tone between phrases, ending on woodwinds alone.

songs.title: 마루에 남은 걸음
songs.genre: Tango with a chamber ensemble arrangement
songs.sub_theme: Bandoneon-led chamber tango, male baritone, danced alone in an empty hall
songs.sp: Tango with a chamber ensemble arrangement, 116 BPM in D minor, 4/4. A bandoneon leads with sharp accented attacks on the first and third beats, opening and closing into long breathy sustains. Violin answers with sliding portamento phrases and biting staccato strokes. The double bass anchors the marcato pulse with sustained root notes under each bar, while the cello takes melodic movement in the lower register, dark and singing beneath the violin. An upright piano hammers percussive block chords on the off-beats and drops chromatic runs into the turnarounds. There is no drum kit; the rhythm is carried by string and piano attacks alone. The harmony leans on minor sixth and diminished passing chords, tense and unresolved. Male baritone vocals sit close and dry, spoken-edged and rhythmic in the verses, opening into full chest voice on the refrain, sung in Korean. Recorded live in an empty hall: natural room reverb, audible bellows noise and floor creak. Dramatic, restrained, aching.

songs.title: 사운드체크
songs.sub_theme: Soundcheck ballad — bare guitar opening into a full-band chorus with doubled vocals
songs.sp: K-Pop power ballad, 76 BPM in F sharp minor, 4/4. Begins with a single clean electric guitar arpeggio through a wide plate reverb and a felted piano playing sparse mid-register voicings. Male tenor vocals enter close and breathy in the lower register, conversational, with audible breath between lines. A synth pad rises under the pre-chorus with soft string samples layered beneath. At the first chorus the full band enters, drums and bass, a tight kick and snare with a little room around them and a fretless bass sliding between roots, and the chorus vocals are doubled an octave apart for width with a third harmony line panned wide. Verse two adds palm-muted guitar and sixteenth-note hi-hat. The bridge drops to piano and voice, then a half-time tom build lifts into the final chorus with crash cymbals, overdriven power chords and a strained belt. The outro decays to clean guitar and a long reverb tail. Korean lyrics throughout.

songs.genre: Bossa nova and Latin jazz fusion
songs.sub_theme: Light bossa-fusion load-out song with muted trumpet, sax trade and scat adlibs
songs.sp: Bossa nova and Latin jazz fusion, 104 BPM in F major, 4/4. A nylon-string guitar comps syncopated bossa patterns built on major seventh and thirteenth voicings, warm and rounded, sitting slightly behind the beat. Electric piano answers with soft tremolo chords and short single-note fills. Fretless electric bass plays a light two-feel, sliding between notes. The drums stay brushed and quiet, cross-stick on the rim with shaker and woodblock keeping the pulse and the hi-hat barely opening. A muted trumpet takes the head, breathy and close-miked, then trades with a tenor saxophone solo over the turnaround. Female vocals sing soft and conversational with almost no vibrato, drifting into scat adlibs over the second chorus and the outro vamp, sung in Korean. Production is warm and analog: ribbon microphone tone, tape saturation, natural room reverb from a large empty hall, wide stereo guitar. Relaxed, sunlit, a little wistful.

songs.title: 다시 문을 열면
songs.genre: Operatic pop ballad with cinematic orchestral arrangements
songs.sub_theme: Operatic finale — piano and soprano opening into full orchestra, choir and driving drums
songs.sp: Operatic pop ballad with cinematic orchestral arrangements, 72 BPM in C minor, 4/4. Opens on a solo grand piano in a large hall, single sustained chords ringing out with the pedal down and room tone audible between them. A female soprano enters in a soft, classically placed head voice, vibrato narrow and controlled, phrasing with rubato. Cellos and low strings swell under the first verse and a boys' choir hums beneath the pre-chorus. The chorus arrives with full band, driving drums, thunderous toms and cymbal crashes under a full string section and brass, with timpani doubling the downbeats. Verse two pulls back to piano, harp and solo violin. The bridge builds through a modulating string ostinato into a key change, and the last chorus carries a massive choir, layered soprano harmonies and soaring operatic adlibs above the melody. Ends on one orchestral hit and a long empty-hall reverb tail. Korean lyrics throughout, sung with operatic diction.
